subject: Re: Pricing: multi-year commitment + partial upfront / Net90 request
messages:
From: Elena Soler <elena@cloudfin.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing / payment terms question for multi-year commit

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo earlier. The leadership team is evaluating a 3-year commitment and we like Redwood's performance profile, but procurement has two asks before we can move to a signed agreement:

- Can we structure partial upfront + milestone payments tied to ramp? Procurement prefers a small upfront (20-30%), then milestones, with the final invoice on Net90.
- They are asking whether Redwood will offer a term discount for multi-year (targeting ~15-20% for a 36-month contract).

Attached is our RFP for context (CloudFin_RFP_May2026.pdf). Can you send a concrete pricing + payment schedule we can show procurement? If Net90 is a hard blocker, let me know what conditions Redwood would need (escrow, letter of credit, stronger SLA, etc.).

Elena
Elena Soler
VP, Platform Partnerships
CloudFin

--
Attachment: CloudFin_RFP_May2026.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soler <elena@cloudfin.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing / payment terms question for multi-year commit

Elena,

Really appreciate the clarity. High-level we can support three pathways — I'll summarize and attach a draft SOW + payment schedule for procurement to review. See attached: Redwood-Draft-SOW-CloudFin-v1.docx and payment_schedule_proposal.xlsx.

1) Annual prepay (recommended for lowest unit price)
   - 12-month prepay, annual renewal; standard hosted SLA; 12% list discount for 12mo prepay.

2) Multi-year ramped prepay (compromise)
   - 36-month term with staged prepay: 30% upfront, 30% at month 12, 40% at month 24 (reduces GAAP impact for you). We can offer a 16% term discount if revenue bands are met each year.

3) Commitment without full prepay (procurement-friendly)
   - 36-month commitment, quarterly invoicing, requires credit approval; discount slightly lower (~10-12%).

About Net90: our standard terms are Net30. We can consider Net60/90 as an exception tied to commercial protections (higher prepay %, escrow, or a letter of credit). If procurement insists on Net90 for the final milestone only and provides stronger upfront, that is workable.

Next steps: If you want, we can circulate a short mutual action plan and I'll loop Lauren (rev ops) to pre-flight a finance exception request.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: Redwood-Draft-SOW-CloudFin-v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), payment_schedule_proposal.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Elena Soler <elena@cloudfin.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim O'Connor <tim.oconnor@finlytics.co>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing / payment terms question for multi-year commit

Karthik,

Thanks — the staged prepay option is closer to what procurement will entertain. A few clarifying asks from our procurement lead:

- Can we move to 30% upfront, 40% at 6 months, remaining 30% at final milestone (final invoice Net90)? That keeps our cashflow flexible.
- For a 36-month commitment we are targeting an 18% term discount (reflects internal cost-of-capital and vendor consolidation plan).
- If Redwood needs additional protections for Net90, would you accept an escrow + signed letter of intent with a mutual termination clause tied to missed SLAs?

Procurement will escalate if we don't have a written approval path for Net90. If you can put an internal approval memo together that lays out the protections Redwood would need, that will help speed things.

Best,
Elena

--
(Quick note: Tim is CloudFin's finance contact; copying him to make sure the payment cadence makes sense from their side.)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pricing / payment terms question for multi-year commit

Team — forwarding CloudFin's ask. They want: 36-month, 30% upfront / 40% @6m / 30% final (final invoice Net90) + target 18% term discount. Procurement will need a finance exception signoff.

Why this is attractive:
- High committed ARR over 3 years and strong reference potential in the finance vertical.
- Staged payments reduce our churn risk vs. pure Net90.

What I'm asking: can we approve a conditional Net90 on the final invoice if CloudFin executes a signed LOI, places 30% upfront, and either: (a) puts 50% of remaining contract value into escrow or (b) provides a letter of credit? I've attached a short memo I plan to share with finance (approval_memo_net90_request.pdf).

Happy to hop on a 20-minute sync if it helps.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Forwarded attachments: approval_memo_net90_request.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing / payment terms question for multi-year commit

Karthik / Lauren — reviewed the memo with finance. We're willing to make a conditional exception given the strategic nature of CloudFin and the contract size, but with tighter protections:

- Accept conditional Net90 on the final milestone only if CloudFin executes both: 30% upfront payment and a Letter of Credit (or escrow) covering 50% of the remaining contract value.
- If LOI + escrow are in place, we can approve an 18% term discount for a 36-month commitment provided that annual revenue bands are met (minimum first-year ARR threshold: $600k).
- If CloudFin prefers not to provide escrow/LOC, alternative is Net60 final with no escrow and a 16% term discount.

Please document these as options in the SOW and have procurement confirm which path they choose. I'm attaching finance-approval-notes.pdf with the rationale.

Markus Klein
VP, Revenue Ops (interim)
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: finance-approval-notes.pdf

From: Elena Soler <elena@cloudfin.ai>

Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing / payment terms question for multi-year commit — acceptance

Karthik / Markus / Lauren — thanks for the quick review. CloudFin accepts the conditional path: we will sign an LOI and arrange an escrow to cover 50% of the remaining value. We agree to the 30% upfront payment and the staged 40% @6m / 30% final structure. We also accept the 18% term discount subject to the first-year ARR threshold you listed.

Please send the SOW and DocuSign package with the escrow instructions and LOI. Procurement will circulate the escrow paperwork to our legal team once we receive the DocuSign envelope. Attaching our signed Letter of Intent for reference (CloudFin-LetterOfIntent-signed.pdf).

Looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Best,
Elena Soler
VP, Platform Partnerships
CloudFin
